input.brief: 把自己的私人相册变成一份能读懂的历年回顾：本地视觉模型逐张读出照片，再写成三种叙事与一份自我画像

direction.name: The contact sheet
direction.idea: Show everything at once, small, in order. The work is laid out like a photographer's contact sheet or an archive drawer: dozens of small frames in strict rows, with all text set at one small size. Nothing is featured, which is the point: the volume and consistency of the body of work is the statement, and the visitor does the choosing. It suits people and studios whose strength is range and output.
direction.composition: The name, or one sentence about the work, sits at display size (6–9vw) across the top of the first screen, and the sheet begins directly under it, still inside the first screen. The first screen opens with three or four short blocks of small text across the top on a 12-column grid (who, what, where to reach them), all at 14–16px, and immediately below, the sheet begins: rows of thumbnails at a fixed height (90–140px) with their natural widths, 6–10px gaps, each project forming a run of four to eight frames preceded by its title in the same small text. The sheet fills the whole page width edge to edge with 16–20px margins. Hovering a run dims the others and shows that project's one-line description in a fixed position. A single enlarged frame may interrupt the sheet once per screen at four times the size.
direction.typography: One face. The name at display size on the first screen; everything else at one text size and one small size; hierarchy below the name comes from position and from a single brighter ink for titles.
direction.colour: Black or white ground, so the thumbnails are the only colour.
direction.imagery: Many images: at least 24 frames to make a sheet. They can be project photographs from the dealt set cropped to mixed ratios, or page captures of the work. Square corners, no captions on the frames.
direction.richness: Density and order. The mass of small images forms a texture; the strict rows keep it calm.
direction.pitfalls: With fewer than about 20 images it looks unfinished; choose another direction. Do not add a big headline above the sheet. On a phone the frames become two per row at a fixed height and each run scrolls sideways. Rows that run past the right edge read as clipped in screenshots and to most visitors: wrap the frames onto the next line, or end each row inside the grid.

hero.name: Text band, then sheet
hero.blueprint: A black or white field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins and 14px gaps. There is no display type: everything is set at one size, 16px, in one weight. The top band is plain text hanging from a line 20px below the top edge: the name in column one; one sentence on availability in column two; a list of five or six services from column three; a longer list of clients or awards from column five; and two links, profile and the single contact action, at the right end of column seven. Lists run one item per line. Below the lists about 300px of ground is left empty. At mid-height the sheet begins: one thumbnail per column, each the full column width (about 190px) at its natural ratio, top-aligned, with the project title in the text size above the first frame of each run of two to four frames. Rows continue below the fold with 40px between them. Frames have square corners and sit directly on the ground with no border and no caption on the image.
hero.mobile: The grid becomes two columns with 12px gaps. The name and the availability sentence take the top; services and clients sit side by side under them as two short lists at 15px. An 80px gap follows, then the sheet: two frames per row at natural ratios, each project title above its first frame. The contact action is a text link fixed bottom-right.
hero.headline: None at display size: the name is set at 16px with the rest of the text, and one sentence of up to 60 characters says what the person does.

type.name: Schibsted Grotesk

display.settings: weight 800 · tracking -0.05em · leading 0.88 · sentence case or all lowercase
display.css:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Schibsted+Grotesk:wght@400;600;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">

text.settings: 400 for paragraphs, 600 for navigation and other functional text · leading 1.4 · tracking -0.01em
text.css:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Schibsted+Grotesk:wght@400;600;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">

type.note: A compact, warm grotesk set heavy with letters almost touching; small text stays in the same family at semibold. Suits music, events and culture pages where the type is the image.

palette.name: Plum-black and pink
palette.note: Near-black and plum at the top and bottom bracket a white middle with navy-black text. Hot pink is reserved for primary buttons, bars in charts and map markers; it never fills a section.

motion.name: Index with preview
motion.description: Rows of text are the navigation through the work; pointing at a row brings up its image in one fixed frame and dims the other rows. On touch screens each row shows its image inline instead. Fast and exact (about 240ms crossfade), no lag behind the pointer. Recipe: 'Index with preview, anchored to the row' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Statement tiles
sections.blueprint: A board of filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8px outer margins: 12 columns by two rows of 38svh each. Tile A, columns 1–8 across both rows, is the darkest tile and carries a slogan of two to four words in capitals at clamp(64px, 9vw, 132px), leading 0.86, on two lines, set hard against the tile's 20px left padding and bottom-aligned. Tile B, columns 9–12 of row one, is a pale tile with one word or figure at the same size, bottom-aligned, cropped by `overflow: hidden` if it runs long. Tile C, columns 9–12 of row two, is a photograph covering the tile. Below the board a fourth tile spans all 12 columns in the page ground colour: its left half is empty and a text of 90–130 words at 22–24px with leading 1.35 runs in columns 7–12 with 40px padding. No separate heading: the slogan in tile A is the heading.
sections.mobile: A two-column board with 6px gaps. The slogan tile spans both columns at 46svh with type at 17vw on two lines; the word tile and the photograph tile sit side by side as squares; the long text tile spans both columns with 20px padding at 18px.

sections.name: Team on colour tiles
sections.blueprint: A one-line heading of two or three words at 28–36px sits top-left; nothing sits to its right. 40px below, a grid of portrait tiles: six columns with 12px gaps across the full content width for 12 or more people, four columns for 4–8. Every tile is a 4:5 photograph treated identically so mixed-quality headshots look like one set: `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.15)` with `mix-blend-mode: multiply` over a flat tint, the tints rotating through four palette colours in a fixed order. Square corners or one small radius. Under each tile, left-aligned to its edge with 10px of space: the name at 15px in full ink and the role at 13px in the soft ink, up to two lines. Rows are 36px apart. A leftover tile in the last row stays at the left; it is not centred. No hover lift and no social icons.
sections.mobile: Two columns with 8px gaps; tiles stay 4:5 with names at 14px beneath. For more than ten people, switch to three columns and show the name only. The heading sits above at 24px. Tints keep their rotation, so the grid reads as a checkerboard of colours.

sections.name: Quiet ledger, side preview
sections.blueprint: A plain ledger in one column 560px wide whose left edge sits at 22% of the viewport width. A heading of two or three words at 24–28px in medium weight, then 32px of space, then one row per project, 44px tall: the name at 16px in full ink at the left, the kind of work at 14px in the soft ink starting at 55% of the column, and the year right-aligned with tabular figures. Nothing is drawn between rows; the three fixed starts make the columns. Hovering or focusing a row keeps it in full ink, drops the others to the soft ink, and shows that project's image in the empty area right of the column: a 4:3 frame 300px wide, `position: absolute`, its top aligned to the hovered row, 64px from the column's right edge, appearing with a 150ms fade. Holds 6–20 rows; group by year with 28px of extra space.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Rows are 52px tall: name at the left, year at the right, kind of work on a second line at 13px. There is no hover preview; instead the first three projects each show a 16:10 image at full column width above their row.

sections.name: Small frames, wide space
sections.blueprint: A flat, quiet viewport 100svh tall in which about 70% of the screen is empty. At mid-height a single row of small portrait frames runs across and off both sides: each frame 11vw wide and 24svh tall (roughly 2:3), spaced 5vw apart, vertically centred, six or seven visible at 1440. Frames have square corners and sit directly on the ground with no border. The row scrolls sideways by drag or trackpad (`overflow-x: auto` with the scrollbar hidden) and may hold 12–24 frames. One line of text overlaps the top-left of the first frame by 12px: a title of two or three words at 20–24px followed by the count, placed above the frame in the stacking order. Hovering a frame scales it to 1.1 from its centre over 250ms; nothing else moves. No captions under frames, no arrows, and no other text in the section.
sections.mobile: The row sits at 45% of an 80svh section. Frames are 34vw wide at 2:3 and 5vw apart, so two and a half are visible and the row scrolls by touch with snapping. The title line sits 20px above the row at the left margin.

sections.name: Quiet figure lines
sections.blueprint: Numbers stated without raising the voice. In columns 2–7, a definition-list layout: three to five rows, each a two-track grid. The first track is 132px wide and holds the figure, right-aligned, at 28–32px in medium weight and full ink with tabular numerals. The second track, after a 24px gap, holds one sentence at 16–17px in the soft ink, at most 40ch, whose first baseline matches the figure's baseline. Sentences share one left edge and figures one right edge, so a clean channel of space runs down between them. 28px between rows. The heading, two to four words at 24–28px, sits 56px above on the sentences' left edge, not the figures'. Optionally, a single small square photograph occupies columns 9–11, its top 80px lower than the first row, with no caption. Leave at least 18vh of empty ground above and below the block.
sections.mobile: The grid stays two-track, with the figure track narrowed to 88px and figures at 24px; sentences at 16px wrap beside them. If the photograph is used it comes after the rows at 56% width, flush right. The heading is 22px on the sentences' left edge.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Smallbits
references.idea: The icon set is the page: a full-viewport wall of the product with one docked card holding every word.
references.hero: The whole viewport is a black field tiled with white pixel icons, each drawn about 50px on a 112px pitch, nine rows deep; alternate rows shift half a cell so it reads as a brick pattern, and icons at the edges are cropped. There is no header. A white square-cornered card, 795×170px, is docked bottom-centre: a two-line 24px semibold sentence left, a black rectangular button right, a row of five grey links below. A third-party badge floats top-right. This single screen is the entire page.
references.type: Inter 600 at 24px, -0.02em, for the one sentence; Inter 16px semibold grey for links and button. Nothing exceeds 1.7vw — the pixel icons, not type, are the display element.
references.colour: #000000 #ffffff #9a9a9a #ff6154 — Strict black and white: white icons on black, black text on a white card, grey for secondary links. The only colour is the coral third-party badge.
references.imagery: About ninety visible pixel icons, each an 8×8 bitmap drawn at 50px in pure white with hard edges, tiled full-bleed and cropped at the viewport edges.
references.layout: One viewport, no scroll. A staggered icon grid fills the frame edge to edge; all words live in one docked card. On mobile the card becomes a full-width white block with a full-width button.

sections.description: Mobile restack, the only other state. The icon wall drops to five columns filling the top 73% of the screen; the card becomes a full-width white block at the bottom with the sentence on three lines at 18px, a full-width black button 78px tall, and five grey links spaced evenly on one line.

steal: Make the product the wallpaper: tile the full viewport with the assets at large size and skip a hero image entirely.
Offset alternate rows by half a cell so a regular grid reads as a pattern rather than a table.
Compress all copy, the CTA and the footer links into one docked card so the page never needs to scroll.

references.name: PROOOOF
references.idea: The product's output is the page: a wall of photos each wearing its coloured EXIF strip, with all the copy folded into one small floating card.
references.hero: The whole viewport is a six-column masonry of photographs on a warm off-white ground with about 15px gutters, columns offset vertically so rows never line up. Each photo has a flat strip fused to its bottom edge carrying tiny monospaced capture data, every strip a different solid colour (black, red, orange, yellow, violet, green). Dead centre floats a white card about 380px wide and 410px tall with roughly 28px corner radius and a soft shadow. It contains an extended wordmark with chained O's, a two-row accordion with the first row open, an App Store badge and a monospaced line of links. There is no navigation.
references.type: An extended, heavy wordmark with interlocked O's is the only display type. Card text is Wintyr VF at about 14-16px, medium weight for accordion headings. EXIF strips and footer links are monospace at roughly 8-13px. No headline anywhere.
references.colour: #f3eee9 #fafafa #191818 #ff6a2b #f7c531 #5a4fcf — Colour comes from the photographs and the saturated caption strips, one hue per photo. Card and gutters stay off-white; a final panel flips to near-black with grey characters.
references.imagery: Casual travel, food, pet and concert photos in mixed portrait and landscape crops, square corners, ungraded, tiled edge to edge. The page ends on an ASCII-art rendering of a hand holding a camera.
references.layout: Effectively a single screen: the photo wall sits behind a centred card that carries every word. Six columns on desktop, two on mobile where the card widens to nearly full width. The only second scene is a dark, inset ASCII panel.

sections.description: All product copy lives in the centred card as an accordion: a row with heading left and chevron right, a hairline divider, the open panel's four-line paragraph, a centred store badge, another divider, a collapsed second row, then a small monospaced line with a version number and underlined links. The card stays put while the wall remains visible on all four sides.

Each tile is a photo with a data strip attached below: two or three rows of monospaced text, four values spread evenly across the first row, date and time at opposite ends of the second, maker and model on the third. Strip and text colours change per tile, for example yellow on black, black on yellow, white on violet, so a uniform grid looks varied.

The closing panel is a near-black rectangle inset with wide margins and filled edge to edge with rows of grey ASCII characters that resolve into a picture of a hand gripping a camera. One line of tiny monospaced uppercase text sits at the exact centre as the call to action. No button and no logo.

steal: Show the product's output at wall scale as the background and confine all copy to one small card on top of it.
Give every repeated tile its own flat accent colour for the caption strip so a strict grid reads as lively.
Hold the explanatory copy in an accordion inside the hero card so the page needs no scrolling.

references.name: Glide Typeface
references.idea: The page background is one grainy sky that passes from midday blue through sunset pink to a starry night as you scroll down the résumé.
references.hero: Full-viewport grainy gradient: saturated sky blue at the top fading through pale pink to warm amber at bottom-left, with soft diagonal cloud streaks. A translucent white pill navigation bar about 62% of the viewport wide floats centred at the top, name at its left and five links at its right. The name is centred at about 33% height in a tight italic display serif at 6.7vw on one line. Beneath it: a two-line sans introduction at roughly 2vw, a white pill button with a blue dot and blue label, then an underlined text link. The lower 35% of the screen is empty gradient.
references.type: editorialOld italic at 96px with -0.02em tracking for the name and section headings, and upright in a narrow cut for one large pull statement; Inter 18px for body, nav and buttons. About a 5:1 jump from display to body. Sentence case, four sizes.
references.colour: #3d9be9 #e8d9d7 #f3d5b8 #6f86d6 #e7b9c4 #1f4a5a — The gradient is the palette: blue to peach, periwinkle with white streaks, pink dusk, then deep teal night. Text flips from near-black to white as it darkens; cobalt is the accent.
references.imagery: No photographs. A full-bleed blurred sky gradient with diagonal cloud streaks and a visible film-grain overlay runs behind the entire page; small white star dots appear in the final night section.
references.layout: One narrow centred column, 45-60% wide, over a continuous background with no section boundaries or colour blocks. Blocks alternate between centred headings with pill buttons and left-aligned text. Experience is a left-rail timeline with glass cards; the footer is a five-column link list.

sections.description: A four-line statement in large upright serif at about 3.5vw, left-aligned inside the centred column, white over the periwinkle part of the sky. It is caught mid-reveal: the first words are fully opaque, the next few half-transparent, the rest at roughly 15% opacity, so the whole paragraph shape is visible before it fills in. Nothing else shares the viewport.

Vertical career timeline. A thin line at the far left of the column carries white-ringed blue dots, each paired with a date range in serif at about 1.6vw. To the right of each dot, a wide frosted-glass card with a 1px light border and rounded corners holds the company name in italic serif, the role in smaller italic, and one line of sans description. Cards are spaced about 150px apart over the pink dusk gradient.

Night sky in deep teal, lightening toward the bottom and scattered with tiny white star dots. A centred italic heading, a three-line centred paragraph and a pale pill button occupy the upper half. Below a faint hairline, five columns of small white links with bold column titles; the first column holds the name and location.

steal: Tie one long background gradient to page position so the palette tells time: day at the hero, dusk mid-page, night with stars at the footer, flipping text from dark to light on the way.
Lay visible grain over a blurred gradient with diagonal streaks so it reads as photographed sky rather than a CSS gradient.
Reveal a large statement word by word on scroll while keeping upcoming words at about 15% opacity, so the paragraph's full shape is present from the start.
